text:
lucy.support: FYI customer (tenant acme-inc) reporting sudden spike of 5xx/timeouts hitting hosted API since ~10:30 PDT. Lots of tail-timeouts from long-context prompts. Escalating to oncall. :rotating_light:

james.cs: Customer says bulk inference job started at ~10:15 and by 10:28 they saw 504s and ~30% error rate. Tenant id: tenant_acme_42. Example request id: rq_7f9b2a3c.

ravi.runtime: Looking at live metrics, I can see their tenant queue depth climb rapidly — continuous-batcher backlog metric (cb.queue_depth) up to 12500 and we hit per-host soft limit at 12k. Active batchers per host ~520, avg batch wait 1.8s -> tail latency spike. Also seeing KV cache cold misses initially.

dan.oncall: Can you paste the gateway logs for rq_7f9b2a3c and the batcher traces? If we confirm queue depth saturation we should enable early-rejects for that tenant and scale dedicated pool if possible.

ravi.runtime: Log snippet for rq_7f9b2a3c:
```
[2025-11-03T17:28:11Z] INFO gateway req=rq_7f9b2a3c ingress: client=acme-inc/120.45.3.8 len=11400 route=/v1/generate
[2025-11-03T17:28:11Z] WARN batcher queue_depth=12487 active_batches=519 wait_ms=1780 kvcache_hit=false
[2025-11-03T17:28:11Z] ERROR handler err=timeout status=504 note="tail timeout (queue depth reached)"
```

megan.sre: I see correlated 504 spikes across a handful of hosts in us-west-2 for that tenant. Autoscaler tried to spin up extra workers but batcher warmup + quantized kernel coldstart gave additional latency so capacity didn't come online fast enough.

james.cs: Customer asked for repro steps, they run a high-concurrency fanout (200 parallel reqs) with long context (30k tokens). How should they throttle?

dan.oncall: Immediate mitigations: 1) apply tenant-level early-reject (drop when queue_depth>8k) 2) enable fallback to smaller model variant for that tenant (reduce per-request resource) 3) add a temporary per-tenant concurrency cap (e.g., 50 concurrent). I'll implement 1 and 3 now.

ravi.runtime: Rolling early-reject policy for tenant_acme_42 -> threshold 8000 (config key: routing.tenants.tenant_acme_42.early_reject). Also added concurrency cap in gateway (max_inflight=50 for tenant).

megan.sre: After changes, metrics look better: queue_depth peaked at 8.2k then fell, 504 rate dropped from 28% -> 3% over 7 mins. No wholesale capacity add required so far. Recommend we still run a controlled repro in staging to validate batching/kv warmup.

james.cs: Customer onboarded to short-term workaround and reduced concurrency on their side. They agree to run a staged ramp with us. :thumbsup:

lucy.support: Repro steps for eng/staging (copied from convo):
- Run 200 parallel curl requests with 30k token prompt to /v1/generate using tenant_acme_42 creds.
- Include header `X-Request-Id: test-ramp-<n>` and measure 95/99 p95/p99 latency and 5xx rate.
Example curl:
```
for i in $(seq 1 200); do
  curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $TENANT_TOKEN" -H "X-Request-Id: test-ramp-$i" -d @long_prompt.json https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate &
done
wait
```

ravi.runtime: Postmortem next steps we discussed: 1) add tenant-aware warmup profile (pre-warm quant kernels based on expected model variant), 2) surface cb.queue_depth in console alerts, 3) tune autoscaler to consider batcher warmup latency. I'll file RFC.

deploy-bot: deploy: rolled tenant early-reject config -> routing.tenants.tenant_acme_42.early_reject=8000 (pr #4921) by dan.oncall at 1754449105.

megan.sre: Closing loop — customer confirms error rate back to normal on their next ramp. We'll keep the tenant cap in place for 48h then revisit after staging repro. Adding action item to incident board.

lucy.support: TL;DR: cause=continuous-batcher backlog + kernel cold starts; immediate fix=tenant early-reject + concurrency cap + fallback variant; next=staging repro + autoscaler/warmup RFC.
